glance_notes.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voter Registration
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: The voter registration deadline for Delaware's November 3, 2026 General Election is Saturday, October 10, 2026.

glance_notes.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voting Locations
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Early Voting: Early voting for Delaware's November 3, 2026 General Election begins October 22 and ends November 1. There is no early voting on October 25.

glance_notes.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Absentee Voting
glance_notes.text: Absentee Voting Requires Eligibility: Delaware does not automatically mail ballots to all voters. Absentee voting is available when a voter qualifies under one of the reasons permitted by Delaware law, with separate protections for military and overseas voters.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Delaware residents can register online through the state's iVote voter portal, by mail, in person at a Department of Elections office, and through designated state agencies. Delaware also uses automatic voter registration through the Division of Motor Vehicles. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, make Delaware your home, and be eligible by age to vote. A person may not register if they have been adjudged mentally incompetent under Delaware's specific legal standard. People convicted of felonies are subject to additional eligibility rules: certain felony convictions permanently disqualify a person, while a person convicted of a non-disqualifying felony may register after completing the sentence as required by Delaware law.
register.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voter Registration
register.internal_note: Primary source establishes registration methods, age/citizenship/residence requirements and felony-registration information. Additional verification source: Delaware Department of Elections Eligibility — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/eligibility.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/eligibility.html) — identifies the mental-competency restriction and disqualifying felony categories. Registration methods and DMV automatic registration are independently documented at [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VoterRegistrationFAQ.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VoterRegistrationFAQ.html). The reader-facing content intentionally does not attempt to make an individual felony-eligibility determination.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Delaware's iVote voter portal to check whether you are registered and review your voter information. You can also contact the Department of Elections to verify your registration.
check_registration.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — iVote Voter Portal
check_registration.internal_note: Supplemental verification source: Delaware Department of Elections Voter Registration — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/votereg.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/votereg.html) — specifically directs voters to iVote to check whether they are registered and also permits verification through the Department.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For Delaware primary and general elections, the regular voter registration deadline is the fourth Saturday before the election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline is Saturday, October 10, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. A mailed voter registration application is timely if it is postmarked by the deadline. Uniformed-service members and citizens living outside the United States have a different deadline; for the 2026 General Election, their registration deadline is October 19, 2026.
deadlines.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voter Registration
deadlines.internal_note: The voter-registration page directly establishes the fourth-Saturday rule, October 10, 2026 deadline at 11:59 p.m., and postmark treatment. Additional verification source: Delaware Department of Elections General Election — [https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/general/general.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/general/general.html) — directly establishes October 19, 2026 as the General Election registration deadline for uniformed-service members and citizens living outside the United States.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: On Election Day, Delaware voters vote at the polling place assigned to their home address. Use the state's iVote voter portal to find your assigned polling place. The Department of Elections also publishes county polling-place lists. Early voting works differently: during the early-voting period, you may vote at any designated early-voting site within your county of residence.
polling_place.glance_value: Find your assigned site with iVote
polling_place.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — iVote Voter Portal
polling_place.internal_note: Supplemental verification sources: Delaware Department of Elections Voting FAQ — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VotingFAQ.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VotingFAQ.html) — establishes assigned Election Day polling places. Ways to Vote — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/waystovote.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/waystovote.html) — establishes that voters may use any early-voting site in their county of residence. Current 2026 polling-place and early-voting listings: [https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/votinglocations.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/votinglocations.html).

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Delaware voters may vote in person at their assigned polling place on Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Use iVote before going to vote if you need to confirm your assigned polling location. Election officers will ask you for proof of identity, but Delaware does not require a photo ID to cast a state or federal election ballot; a voter on the poll list who does not show identification can use the state's Affirmation of Voter Identity procedure.
election_day.glance_value: Vote at your assigned polling place
election_day.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — 2026 General Election
election_day.internal_note: Primary source establishes the November 3 election, assigned-polling-place process through iVote, and 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. hours. Supplemental verification source for identification procedure: Delaware Department of Elections Voting FAQ — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VotingFAQ.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VotingFAQ.html).

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Delaware polling places are open from 7:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. for general, primary and special elections. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, polls are open statewide from 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.
polling_hours.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — 2026 General Election
polling_hours.internal_note: The official General Election page directly establishes 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. for November 3, 2026. The Department's Voting FAQ — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VotingFAQ.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/VotingFAQ.html) — independently states that polling places are open 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. for General, Primary and Special elections.

early_voting.label: Early Voting
early_voting.content: Delaware offers in-person early voting at designated sites within each county. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting is available October 22 through October 24 from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.; there is no early voting October 25; voting resumes October 26 and October 27 from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.; and October 28 through November 1 hours are 11:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. During early voting, you may vote at any designated early-voting site in your county of residence.
early_voting.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voting Locations
early_voting.internal_note: The current official Voting Locations page directly establishes the 2026 General Election early-voting dates, the October 25 closure, daily hours and currently confirmed locations. Additional verification source: Delaware Department of Elections Ways to Vote — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/waystovote.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/waystovote.html) — establishes that voters may use any early-voting site in their county of residence. The Department currently notes that a Sussex County General Election storefront location remains to be determined, so voters should use the live location page rather than a static list.

absentee_mail.label: Absentee & Mail Voting
absentee_mail.content: Delaware absentee voting is available to voters who cannot go to their polling place on Election Day for a reason allowed under Delaware law, as well as qualifying military and overseas voters. The quickest way to request an absentee ballot is through iVote; voters may also submit the official application to the Department of Elections. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, October 30 is the last day for the Department to mail an absentee ballot, and November 2 at noon is the deadline for the Department to issue one. A completed absentee ballot must reach the Department of Elections office for the voter's county by 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. Absentee ballots cannot be returned at an early-voting site or Election Day polling place.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Excuse required; ballot due by 8 p.m. Election Day
absentee_mail.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: Primary source establishes iVote and paper application methods, county return offices and 8:00 p.m. Election Day receipt deadline. Additional verification source: Delaware Department of Elections General Election — [https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/general/general.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/general/general.html) — establishes October 30 as the last day to submit a request in time for the ballot to be mailed and November 2 at noon as the Department's issuance deadline. Ways to Vote — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/waystovote.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/waystovote.html) — expressly states that absentee ballots cannot be returned to early-voting sites or polling places. Eligibility is excuse-based; this is not universal vote-by-mail.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Delaware election officers ask voters voting in person to show proof of identity, but Delaware does not require a photo ID to vote in state and federal elections. The state does not have a single closed list of acceptable identification. Examples include a Delaware driver's license or state identification card, a Department of Elections mailing, current utility bill, bank statement, lease or deed, vehicle registration or title, government mailing, or other government documentation showing the voter's name and current Delaware address. If you do not show identification, are at the correct polling place or an early-voting site, and appear on the poll list, you may complete an Affirmation of Voter Identity and then vote.
voter_id.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voting FAQ
voter_id.internal_note: Primary source directly states that photo ID is not required, that Delaware does not have a defined list of acceptable forms of identification, and that a voter without ID can complete an Affirmation of Voter Identity when otherwise eligible. Additional verification source: Delaware Department of Elections Election Security FAQ — [https://elections.delaware.gov/public/faq/security.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/public/faq/security.html) — provides examples of identification and states that election officers ask for one form showing name and current Delaware address. Registration ID requirements are separate and are not conflated with this section.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Delaware provides accessible polling places, accessible voting machines and voting assistance for voters with disabilities. The state's ExpressVote XL voting machines include accessibility features such as an audio-tactile keypad with Braille legends. Voters who need assistance may tell an election officer or bring someone to help with the voting process. Delaware also provides accessible absentee voting. Certain voters who are sick or temporarily or permanently physically disabled may request electronic delivery and return of an absentee ballot in a format compatible with accessibility software.
accessible_voting.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Voters With Disabilities
accessible_voting.internal_note: Primary source establishes accessible polling places, accessible machines, assistance and ExpressVote XL accessibility features. Supplemental verification source for accessible electronic absentee ballot delivery and return: Delaware Department of Elections Absentee Voting — [https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/absentee/](https://elections.delaware.gov/voter/absentee/).

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Delaware provides special registration and absentee-voting procedures for uniformed-service members, eligible family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. These voters can use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request an absentee ballot. Delaware also permits qualifying voters to request permanent absentee status. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup when there is not enough time to receive a regular ballot or the requested ballot does not arrive. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the voter registration deadline for uniformed-service members and citizens living outside the United States is October 19, 2026.
military_overseas.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Uniformed and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Primary source establishes covered voter categories, FPCA registration/ballot request, permanent absentee status and FWAB use. Supplemental verification source for the October 19, 2026 registration deadline: Delaware Department of Elections General Election — [https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/general/general.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/general/general.html). Official forms page — [https://elections.delaware.gov/public/forms/](https://elections.delaware.gov/public/forms/) — provides both the FPCA and FWAB.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A Delaware resident attending college away from home can remain registered at their Delaware home address. If the student cannot vote at their assigned Delaware polling place on Election Day, Delaware specifically recognizes students within its absentee-voting framework. The Department recommends requesting an absentee ballot as soon as the student knows the address where the ballot should be sent for the fall semester. Students should keep their voter registration and mailing information current through the Department of Elections.
student_voting.glance_value: Delaware students away at school may vote absentee
student_voting.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — College Students
student_voting.internal_note: Primary source specifically addresses Delaware citizens attending college and directs registered students who cannot vote at their Election Day polling place to use Delaware's absentee process. Delaware's official absentee materials identify students under the business-or-occupation absentee reason. This section deliberately does not assert that an out-of-state student attending school in Delaware automatically establishes Delaware voting residence; the official student page does not establish that broader claim.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: The Delaware Department of Elections publishes official sample ballots for state elections. Sample ballots vary by election district and, for a primary, by political party. Use the Department's current election page or iVote to find ballot information when it becomes available. As of August 30, 2026, the Department states that sample ballots for the November 3, 2026 General Election are not yet available.
sample_ballot.glance_value: 2026 General sample ballots not yet posted
sample_ballot.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — 2026 General Election
sample_ballot.internal_note: The current General Election page expressly states that 2026 General Election sample ballots are not yet available. The Department is already publishing official district-specific sample ballots for the September 15, 2026 Primary, confirming its sample-ballot publication process. Reverify this section after General Election sample ballots are posted.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Delaware Department of Elections, Office of the State Election Commissioner, 905 S. Governors Avenue, Suite 170, Dover, DE 19904. Phone: 302-739-4277. Fax: 302-739-6794. Email: COE_Vote@delaware.gov. Regular office hours are weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Delaware also maintains separate Department of Elections offices for Kent, New Castle and Sussex counties.
contact.source_name: Delaware Department of Elections — Offices & Contact Information
contact.internal_note: The current official locations page directly verifies the State Election Commissioner office address, phone, fax, weekday operating hours and county office structure. The email address is displayed by the live page in protected form; the current official 2026 candidate filing packet independently prints [COE_Vote@delaware.gov](mailto:COE_Vote@delaware.gov): [https://elections.delaware.gov/candidates/campaignfinance/pdfs/candidate_filing_packet.pdf](https://elections.delaware.gov/candidates/campaignfinance/pdfs/candidate_filing_packet.pdf).

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Delaware Department of Elections website for statewide election information and iVote for voter registration, registration lookup, polling-place information and absentee-ballot services. The Department maintains county offices for Kent, New Castle and Sussex counties and publishes current voting locations, election calendars, forms and voter guidance. Municipal elections can have different voter qualifications and procedures under individual city and town charters, so voters participating in a municipal election should also check directly with that municipality.
official_resources.glance_value: Department of Elections, iVote & county offices
official_resources.internal_note: Official voter portal: [https://ivote.de.gov/](https://ivote.de.gov/). Official 2026 Election Calendar: [https://elections.delaware.gov/public/calendar/pdfs/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf](https://elections.delaware.gov/public/calendar/pdfs/2026ElectionCalendar.pdf). Official voting locations: [https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/votinglocations.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/elections/votinglocations.html). Official forms: [https://elections.delaware.gov/public/forms/](https://elections.delaware.gov/public/forms/). Official offices and county contacts: [https://elections.delaware.gov/locations.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/locations.html). Official municipal-election portal: [https://elections.delaware.gov/municipality/](https://elections.delaware.gov/municipality/). Department FAQ — [https://elections.delaware.gov/public/faq/faqs.html](https://elections.delaware.gov/public/faq/faqs.html) — expressly warns that city and town charters determine voter qualifications for municipal elections.
